pairs.subject: retry-backoff
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/e2e/budget_terminal.rs:161 The contract test pins a DataHub cost:pause governance hold (a local, caller-side precondition the worker knew before running) as a terminal Failed job that consumes one attempt, so the work is not held as suspended and is not owed a result once the hold lifts; the operator must re-enqueue.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/e2e/budget_terminal.rs:161 The governance-hold test asserts attempts == 1 with status Failed; the technique's check is that a blocked attempt increments no failure count and the work stays suspended with the precondition named (the name is realized, the suspension is not).

crates/server/src/e2e/budget_terminal.rs:80 Budget exhaustion is pinned as permanent: exactly one attempt spent and the remaining attempts left visibly unburned instead of a retry ladder against a refusal that cannot heal.

crates/server/src/e2e/panic_containment.rs:100 A failed attempt with attempts remaining is re-queued with a persisted available_at later than creation, i.e. the retry-at is a row, not a sleeping task.

pairs.registryProposal: suspension-is-not-failure names offline, missing credential, backgrounded and lease-not-held as suspension, and storm-control calls policy outcomes denials. An operator-imposed governance hold (a cost:pause tag) sits between the two; the technique should state whether such a hold suspends the work or is a terminal policy denial with the hold named, since pumper deliberately chose the latter.

pairs.subject: retry-backoff
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/webhook.rs:1042 A receiver's Retry-After is truncated to 5 s for the next in-process attempt, so a stated 300 s wait is answered with a request at 5 s (and the drain ladder's 30 s first rung is also earlier than stated); backoff-design requires honouring the stated wait or ending with an over-budget-wait terminal carrying the stated delay.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/webhook.rs:1042 next_sleep = ra.min(RETRY_AFTER_INPROC_CAP) shortens the dependency's stated schedule rather than honouring it or stopping; the in-process default ladder at webhook.rs:997 is also unjittered (2 s, 4 s).

crates/server/src/webhook.rs:89 Every status that is not 2xx or 4xx (including unexpected 3xx/1xx) falls into Transient; there is no separately counted unknown class, so a novel failure is silently filed as retryable.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:3166 A failed delivery's next attempt is persisted as next_retry_at on the row with up to +25% jitter, so the drain ladder survives restarts.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:3194 kill_delivery (permanent rejection) writes the same status 'dead' as the exhaustion branch of fail_delivery, so reclassified and exhausted are distinguishable only through last_error prose.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/cache.rs:525 The context is mostly an HTTP response cache, but it also owns the Claude research-response cache whose key digests the prompt, the appended system prompt, role/model/effort, max_turns and schema and is extended with the researcher's answer fingerprint; that realizes one technique, while the other 31 presuppose an assembler this context does not own, so the evidence floor (16 of 32) cannot be met and not-applicable would be false.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/cache.rs:499 The cached-answer key hashes the full standing text (append_system_prompt) beside the prompt, separated canonically, and key_with (cache.rs:525) folds in the resolved model/effort/tools fingerprint so a config edit starts a fresh key; resume_session requests bypass the cache.

pairs.registryProposal: The conform evidence floor counts all of a subject's techniques. A context that legitimately owns one technique of a 32-technique subject (here a model-response cache) can never be conformant and is wrong as not-applicable; the floor should count applicable techniques, with not-applicable ones anchored once collectively.
